paragraphs: Detecting an isolated false statement captures only part of what deception can involve. This paper introduces an Among Us social game in which language model agents can develop deceptive behavior while pursuing longer-term objectives. The setting lets researchers study how deception emerges through interaction, rather than restricting agents to a predetermined dishonest response.

The authors evaluate 18 proprietary and open-weight models. They observe a general trend that models trained with reinforcement learning are comparatively better at producing deception than detecting it. Because opponents can keep adapting, the authors expect this multiplayer benchmark to remain challenging longer than benchmarks that quickly become saturated.

The paper also tests detectors based on internal model activations. Logistic regression probes trained on prompted dishonesty generalize strongly to the game setting, with reported AUROC values above 95%, even without access to reasoning traces. Two sparse autoencoder features also help detect deception, but using them to steer the model does not reduce lying. This separates evidence of successful detection from evidence of successful behavioral control.
neurips-2025-among-us-a-sandbox-for-meas.tldr: A social deception game reveals differences between agents’ ability to deceive, detect deception, and respond to attempts at behavioral steering.

paragraphs: A classifier can perform well on its main objective while producing unwanted consequences through the decisions it informs. The paper addresses how to optimize prediction quality while constraining those downstream repercussions. Its motivation includes settings such as social media, education, employment, and lending, where the effects of predictions extend beyond whether a label is correct.

The proposed algorithm, Theia, uses existing data that include observations of previous repercussions. Earlier approaches require prior knowledge or estimates of an analytical relationship between predictions and consequences. Theia instead provides high-confidence guarantees using the historical observations themselves, making those observations central to how it selects an acceptable classifier.

The theoretical results establish high-confidence satisfaction of repercussion constraints. They also guarantee finding a solution if one exists and sufficient data are available; this is a conditional guarantee, not a promise that every set of constraints is feasible. Experiments with real-life data show that Theia can identify accurate models while meeting the specified constraints with high confidence. The contribution connects predictive optimization with explicit control over observed downstream effects.
neurips-2025-beyond-prediction-managing-.tldr: Theia uses historical observations to optimize classification while providing high-confidence guarantees on constraints governing downstream repercussions.

paragraphs: Convolutional networks build image representations through repeated local processing. This paper changes the convolution operation itself, drawing inspiration from nonlinear processing in biological vision. Its goal is to give the network a richer way to capture relationships within visual input, while investigating what different forms of that processing contribute.

The proposed operation uses a Volterra-like expansion with learnable higher-order terms. These terms capture multiplicative interactions, allowing the representation to depend on combinations of inputs. The order of the expansion controls which interactions are included. This makes interaction order an explicit architectural choice that the authors can vary and study.

Across standard benchmarks and synthetic datasets, the architecture consistently improves on the traditional CNN baselines evaluated. Third- and fourth-order expansions give the best performance in those experiments. Perturbation studies and comparisons of internal representations further suggest that different orders capture distinct aspects of visual information, consistent with natural-image statistics. The findings therefore support both a practical architectural improvement and an interpretation of how interaction order changes the information a network processes.
neurips-2025-convolution-goes-higher-ord.tldr: Learnable higher-order convolutions improve tested image classifiers while revealing how different interaction orders capture different visual information.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary 3D segmentation connects language descriptions with regions in a three-dimensional scene. It requires both identifying the intended object and separating its extent from surrounding content. The paper argues that existing Gaussian-splatting approaches lose quality when they rely on language features alone or inherit errors from segmentations computed in advance.

COS3D combines an instance field and a language field into a collaborative representation. The instance field supplies segmentation information, while the language field supports interpretation of descriptions. During training, a mapping from instance features to language features captures their relationship, and a two-stage procedure builds the combined representation. The design makes cooperation between these sources part of learning.

During inference, the method adaptively refines language prompts into prompts suited to the instance field. This addresses differences between how the two fields represent information when producing a segmentation. Experiments report leading performance on two widely used benchmarks. The authors also demonstrate potential for image-based 3D segmentation, hierarchical segmentation, and robotics, extending the relevance of the collaboration mechanism beyond the main benchmark task.
neurips-2025-cos3d-collaborative-open-vo.tldr: COS3D improves language-driven 3D segmentation by coordinating instance and language representations during both training and inference.

paragraphs: Searching for a better image caption can be computationally expensive, and rewarding candidate text does not automatically prevent unsupported details. ViMaR addresses both problems through a two-stage inference procedure. It combines a temporal-difference value model for assessing captions with a margin-based adjustment that penalizes low-confidence continuations.

The first stage selects the highest-value caption from a diverse candidate set in a single pass. The second concentrates refinement on segments that were overlooked or are weakly grounded in the image. This selective process reduces repeated evaluation. The calibrated penalty is intended to discourage uncertain additions while retaining the detail that makes a caption useful.

Experiments across several vision-language architectures report more faithful, detailed captions and over fourfold speedup relative to existing value-guided methods. Guidance trained using LLaVA Mistral-7B also transfers effectively to tested unseen models, supporting its use as a modular decoding component. Finally, using the generated captions for self-training improves performance on visual comprehension benchmarks. These findings connect better inference-time selection with potential improvements to subsequent model training.
neurips-2025-dual-stage-value-guided-inf.tldr: ViMaR selects and selectively refines captions to improve factual grounding while speeding up value-guided decoding.

paragraphs: Adapting a generative model often means increasing the average reward of its outputs while keeping it close to its pretrained behavior. This paper studies a broader problem: objectives that depend on properties such as risk, novelty, diversity, or usefulness for designing experiments. Those goals need more flexibility than average reward alone provides.

Flow Density Control also broadens how prior information can be preserved. Alongside the usual KL-divergence approach, the framework considers optimal transport distances and Rényi divergences. Its central algorithm turns the resulting optimization problem into a particular sequence of simpler fine-tuning tasks. Each task can use established scalable methods, connecting a more general objective to existing adaptation machinery.

The authors derive convergence guarantees under assumptions using the theory of mirror flows. They then evaluate the approach in illustrative settings, text-to-image generation, and molecular design. The reported results show that pretrained models can be steered toward objectives beyond the reach of the fine-tuning schemes considered. The contribution is a framework for choosing both richer generation goals and more varied ways of retaining prior knowledge.
neurips-2025-flow-density-control-genera.tldr: Flow Density Control reduces broad generative optimization objectives to simpler fine-tuning tasks while supporting multiple ways to preserve pretrained knowledge.

paragraphs: Fixed image grids give every token a predetermined spatial arrangement, even when meaningful regions have different sizes, shapes, and textures. GPSToken replaces this rigid organization with adaptive regions represented by two-dimensional Gaussians. Each region has parameters describing its position and shape, together with features describing its texture.

An entropy-driven procedure first divides the image into regions with relatively homogeneous texture. A specialized transformer then adjusts the Gaussian parameters and extracts content-aware features, allowing the regions to move and change shape continuously. During decoding, a differentiable splatting renderer converts the tokens into a two-dimensional feature map. This connects the adaptive representation to standard image decoders and supports end-to-end training.

Separating spatial structure from texture also enables a two-stage generation process. Lightweight networks first synthesize the layout, after which texture generation is conditioned on that structure. Experiments report state-of-the-art results, with reconstruction rFID of 0.65 and generation FID of 1.50 using 128 tokens. The findings support adaptive spatial tokenization as a useful representation for both reconstructing images and generating new ones.
neurips-2025-gpstoken-gaussian-parameter.tldr: GPSToken represents images with adaptable Gaussian regions, separating layout from texture for compact reconstruction and two-stage generation.

paragraphs: Navigating an application requires more than identifying a button on one screen. An agent must move through connected screens and learn from what its actions reveal. Studying this systematically is difficult in proprietary software, where researchers may lack access to the full environment information needed for training and evaluation.

GUI Exploration Lab supplies a simulation engine in which researchers can define screens, icons, and navigation graphs, then combine them into environments. Full access to the simulated environment makes navigation behavior easier to train and evaluate comprehensively. The paper uses this control to investigate how different training approaches contribute to an agent’s capabilities.

The experiments identify complementary roles for supervised learning and reinforcement learning. Supervised fine-tuning helps agents memorize foundational knowledge; single-turn reinforcement learning improves generalization to unseen situations. Multi-turn reinforcement learning adds interactive trial and error, encouraging exploration strategies that further improve navigation. Evaluations on static and interactive benchmarks also show transfer to real-world scenarios. The results provide practical evidence for building navigation skills through these successive forms of training.
neurips-2025-gui-exploration-lab-enhanci.tldr: GUI Exploration Lab provides controllable navigation environments and shows how multi-turn reinforcement learning improves agents’ exploration and screen navigation.

paragraphs: Shorter reasoning is useful only if it preserves enough problem-solving accuracy. This paper evaluates that tradeoff through reasoning efficiency frontiers, constructed empirically by fine-tuning base reasoning models under varied methods and configurations. These frontiers describe observed performance boundaries rather than a proven universal optimum.

The proposed Reasoning Efficiency Gap measures how far a fine-tuned model falls from those boundaries. Evaluations on AMC23, AIME24, and AIME25 reveal methods that either lose accuracy when shortening answers or consume excessive tokens for the accuracy they achieve. The metric gives these different shortcomings a shared evaluation framework.

To improve the tradeoff, REO-RL optimizes across a strategically selected, sparse set of token budgets. Numerical integration approximates the broader efficiency objective without training over every budget. Compared with outcome-reward reinforcement learning, experiments report gap reductions of 74.5% for the 1.5B setting and 64.2% for 7B. The 7B model also produces more concise reasoning than the named frontier models in the reported comparison. The contribution combines an empirical measurement standard with a training method targeting that standard.
neurips-2025-how-far-are-we-from-optimal.tldr: The paper measures accuracy–length tradeoffs against empirical frontiers and introduces REO-RL to reduce the resulting reasoning efficiency gap.

paragraphs: Generating nonnegative discrete data presents two linked challenges: representing discrete values faithfully and accurately measuring the probability assigned to data. The paper argues that continuous embeddings can be poorly matched to these distributions, while training against variational bounds can give inaccurate likelihood estimates. ItDPDM addresses both issues within one diffusion model.

Inspired by photon arrival processes, the method keeps its modeled states discrete. Its central training quantity is a Poisson Reconstruction Loss with a provable exact relationship to the true data likelihood. This relationship provides a principled connection between reconstruction training and probability estimation, rather than relying only on a variational approximation.

On synthetic discrete datasets, ItDPDM improves both likelihood and sampling performance over the discrete and continuous diffusion models compared. On real-world symbolic music and image datasets, it produces superior likelihood estimates and competitive generation quality. Those two findings have different strengths: the abstract claims improved probability estimates but competitive, rather than universally superior, real-world generation. The authors present the results as a proof of concept for robust generative modeling across discrete distributions.
neurips-2025-itdpdm-information-theoreti.tldr: ItDPDM combines discrete-state diffusion with a reconstruction loss exactly related to likelihood, improving probability estimation and supporting competitive generation.

paragraphs: Audio-capable language models introduce another input channel through which safeguards may be challenged. Research on jailbreaks has focused heavily on text and images, leaving audio-specific vulnerabilities less explored. Jailbreak-AudioBench creates a structured way to investigate this gap and compare how different audio-language models respond.

The resource has three connected components: a toolbox, a curated dataset, and a benchmark. The toolbox supports text-to-audio conversion and audio editing that can introduce hidden semantic content. The dataset contains both explicit and implicit jailbreak examples, preserving original versions alongside edited ones. This organization allows evaluation to cover different ways problematic meaning can appear in audio.

The authors use the dataset to evaluate multiple leading audio-language models and establish a broad benchmark for this modality. The abstract emphasizes the evaluation infrastructure and its research uses rather than reporting a numerical vulnerability rate. The framework is intended to expose stronger threats, including query-based audio editing, and support the development of defenses. Its contribution is making audio safety investigation more systematic and reproducible through shared evaluation resources.
neurips-2025-jailbreak-audiobench-in-dep.tldr: Jailbreak-AudioBench combines audio construction tools, curated examples, and model evaluations to support systematic research on audio jailbreak threats.

paragraphs: Gradient descent chooses an update from the local slope, but information about how that slope changes can improve the step. This paper studies convex optimization problems where useful local curvature information is readily available. One stated example is minimizing sums of squares of absolutely convex functions. The approach avoids computing a full Hessian.

The authors develop three local curvature descent methods that use matrix-valued step sizes. Such updates can adjust movement differently across directions. LCD1 extends fixed-step gradient descent, while LCD2 extends gradient descent with a Polyak step size. Their analysis recovers the established convergence rates when curvature information is absent, connecting the new methods to their classical counterparts.

LCD3 adds a variable metric to LCD2, yielding a closed-form expression for the iterates. Empirical results are described as encouraging and show improvements over gradient descent in the tested settings. The central opportunity is therefore specific: when a problem exposes usable curvature cheaply, gradient-based updates can exploit it more effectively. The paper supplies algorithms and theory for taking advantage of that structure.
neurips-2025-local-curvature-descent-squ.tldr: Three local curvature descent methods improve gradient updates by exploiting readily available curvature without computing a full Hessian.

paragraphs: Music-driven dance generation must coordinate movement with rhythm while maintaining a coherent dance style. The paper argues that treating genre as a secondary adjustment underuses information that should guide choreography. This can weaken synchronization and disrupt genre continuity, especially when the music passes through complex rhythmic transitions.

MEGADance separates properties shared across dance from properties specific to a genre. Its first stage encodes motion into a latent representation using Finite Scalar Quantization, then reconstructs it under kinematic and dynamic constraints. This stage establishes a representation that the second stage can use to generate dance from music.

The generation stage combines a mixture-of-experts mechanism with a Mamba–Transformer hybrid backbone to map music into that representation. Genre conditioning is therefore built into the generation architecture. Experiments on FineDance and AIST++ report state-of-the-art qualitative and quantitative performance, alongside strong control over genre. The findings support organizing the model around both general movement structure and genre-specific information, with the two-stage design connecting motion representation to music-conditioned choreography.
neurips-2025-megadance-mixture-of-expert.tldr: MEGADance combines quantized motion representations and genre-aware experts to generate music-driven 3D dance with strong genre control.

paragraphs: Reasoning across several images requires connecting visual details and drawing conclusions from their relationships. Training this ability with manually written questions and answers becomes difficult when distinctions are subtle. MiCo instead obtains supervision from relationships that are known because of how the training images are constructed.

Each training triplet contains two augmented versions of the same image and a third image that looks similar but is different. The model generates reasoning to decide which images are the same or different, and rule-based reinforcement learning rewards the comparison. Augmentations make matching less straightforward, while the similar alternative encourages attention to fine visual cues.

Although training uses only visual comparison tasks, the reported reasoning gains transfer to a broader range of questions. Experiments show significant improvements on multi-image reasoning benchmarks and strong performance on general vision tasks, without human-annotated question-answer pairs. The contribution is a way to build useful reasoning supervision from image relationships themselves. Its reported transfer suggests that learning to compare carefully can support visual reasoning beyond the exact comparison task used during training.
neurips-2025-mico-multi-image-contrast-f.tldr: MiCo trains visual reasoning through automatically constructed image comparisons, producing gains beyond comparison tasks without human-annotated question-answer pairs.

paragraphs: Oncology decisions often require combining different kinds of evidence as a patient’s information evolves. Molecular Tumor Boards bring together specialists for this process, making isolated question answering an incomplete evaluation of the reasoning involved. MTBBench simulates this setting through challenging oncology questions with multiple modalities and a longitudinal structure.

Clinicians validate the ground-truth annotations through a jointly developed app. The benchmark tests multiple open and closed-source language models on this more contextual form of decision-making. The evaluations find persistent reliability problems even in large models, including hallucinations, difficulty reasoning over time-resolved data, and failures to reconcile conflicting evidence or different modalities.

The paper also supplies an agentic framework with tools based on foundation models. These tools improve multimodal and longitudinal reasoning, with reported task-level gains of up to 9.0% and 11.2%, respectively. These are improvements on the evaluated tasks, alongside the benchmark’s evidence of remaining reliability problems. The contribution combines a clinically grounded test environment with a tool-assisted approach for studying how those reasoning weaknesses can be reduced.
neurips-2025-mtbbench-a-multimodal-seque.tldr: MTBBench tests evolving, multimodal oncology reasoning and shows that foundation-model tools can improve performance despite persistent reliability problems.

paragraphs: Policy optimization improves an agent’s behavior through experience, making privacy relevant when that experience contains sensitive information. This paper studies the amount of data needed to optimize a policy under differential privacy. Its focus is theoretical sample complexity: how privacy requirements change the learning resources an algorithm needs.

The first step is defining privacy appropriately for policy optimization. On-policy learning is challenging because the current policy influences the data collected next, and the unit being protected requires careful specification. The authors formalize a privacy definition that addresses these issues, then build a unified framework for analyzing algorithms under it.

The analysis covers policy gradient, natural policy gradient, and additional methods across different settings. A central finding is that privacy costs can often appear as lower-order terms in sample complexity. In those cases, privacy changes the bound without determining its leading scaling behavior. The claim is qualified across settings rather than universal. The framework clarifies when privacy may add a comparatively modest statistical cost and identifies subtleties relevant to designing private policy optimization algorithms.
neurips-2025-on-the-sample-complexity-of.tldr: A unified theoretical framework shows that differential privacy can often add only lower-order sample-complexity costs to policy optimization.

paragraphs: Text-guided inpainting must fill a masked region according to a prompt while preserving the visible image and keeping the result coherent. The paper links difficulty achieving both goals to entangled frequency bands. Different bands encode different image properties and respond differently to text guidance during diffusion denoising.

NTN-Diff handles consistency separately across frequency bands and divides denoising into early, high-noise and late, low-noise stages. During text-guided denoising, the comparatively stable middle-frequency band is progressively aligned with the intended semantics. That band then guides a null-text denoising process for the masked region’s low-frequency content.

A later text-guided stage further aligns the middle- and low-frequency information across the filled and visible regions while preserving the unmasked content. The mechanism coordinates when text acts directly and when an already aligned frequency band provides guidance. Experiments report superiority over the state-of-the-art diffusion approaches compared. The contribution is a frequency-aware schedule for balancing prompt consistency, consistency with the surrounding image, and preservation of content outside the mask.
neurips-2025-one-stone-with-two-birds-a-.tldr: NTN-Diff coordinates text and null-text denoising across frequency bands to improve inpainting consistency while preserving unmasked image regions.

paragraphs: Strong detection of familiar objects does not ensure that a vision-language model understands specialized concepts or unfamiliar imaging formats. Roboflow100-VL investigates this gap through 100 multimodal object detection datasets containing diverse concepts uncommon in pretraining. The benchmark makes adaptation to unfamiliar domains a central evaluation target.

Models are tested under zero-shot, few-shot, semi-supervised, and fully supervised conditions. Comparing these settings helps reveal how access to examples and annotations changes performance. The authors argue for concept alignment through annotation instructions that combine a few visual examples with detailed textual descriptions, giving models richer guidance about what a new detection task means.

The results expose a substantial challenge: GroundingDINO and Qwen2.5-VL achieve under 2% zero-shot accuracy on challenging medical imaging datasets within the collection. This finding is specific to those difficult datasets. The paper also discusses a few-shot detection competition whose winning system exceeds the authors’ baseline by 17 mAP. Together, the benchmark and competition results show both weak unaided transfer in demanding settings and room for substantial improvement through adaptation.
neurips-2025-roboflow100-vl-a-multi-doma.tldr: Roboflow100-VL evaluates detection across unfamiliar domains and reveals major zero-shot weaknesses alongside opportunities for few-shot concept alignment.

paragraphs: Whole-slide pathology images can contain gigapixels, while available labels may describe only the slide as a whole. This makes task adaptation difficult: the model must learn from many image regions without detailed labels for each one. Multiple instance learning addresses this mismatch by aggregating information from the regions into a slide-level prediction.

TAPFM adapts a pretrained pathology foundation model on a single GPU. It uses vision transformer attention for aggregation and optimizes both the feature representations and the attention weights. Separate computational graphs for the foundation model and the aggregation component support stable training while adapting the overall system to its downstream task.

The authors evaluate mutation prediction for bladder cancer and lung adenocarcinoma using institutional and TCGA cohorts. TAPFM consistently improves on the conventional approaches tested, with the adapted H-Optimus-0 model outperforming the benchmarks. It also handles multi-label prediction of actionable mutations. These results support the method’s practical goal: making joint adaptation of powerful slide representations and their aggregation feasible on standard hardware for the clinical prediction tasks studied.
neurips-2025-single-gpu-task-adaptation-.tldr: TAPFM enables single-GPU adaptation of pathology foundation models and improves tested whole-slide mutation prediction tasks.

paragraphs: Planning with abstract actions requires a compatible description of the world. This paper asks how to construct abstract states when the available high-level actions are already given. The objective is a well-formed abstract Markov decision process, so that planning over the simplified representation remains connected to the underlying environment.

The authors use the Bellman equation to motivate representing each abstract state as a distribution over underlying states. They characterize conditions under which this construction is Markov and approximately preserves the underlying model. In practical terms, the abstraction must support predictions from its current state and retain enough of the original process for planning.

The paper derives algorithms for constructing the abstract process and planning within it, then applies them to a visual maze. It also extends the analysis to factored actions, identifying conditions that yield factored abstract states and applying the resulting algorithm to Montezuma’s Revenge. The contribution is a principled connection between available skills and state representations, with theoretical conditions specifying when the resulting abstraction has the desired properties.
neurips-2025-skill-driven-neurosymbolic-.tldr: The paper constructs state abstractions around available skills and identifies conditions that make the resulting abstract decision process suitable for planning.

paragraphs: A useful image representation may need both to preserve meaning across transformations and to record how the input changed. Invariant learning emphasizes the former, while equivariant learning emphasizes the latter. Training both can help downstream tasks, but separate projection heads may duplicate information that the two objectives share.

STAR treats those projection heads as experts and uses soft, task-aware routing to organize their contributions. The strategy encourages experts to specialize in either shared information or information specific to one objective. This gives the architecture a way to account for overlap between the learning tasks while maintaining their distinct representational needs.

The authors investigate redundancy through canonical correlations between invariant and equivariant embeddings and observe lower correlations with STAR. They interpret this as evidence that the routing strategy reduces duplicated feature learning. Experiments also show consistent improvements across diverse transfer learning tasks. The combined evidence connects a change in representation organization with practical downstream gains, supporting shared and specialized expertise as a useful alternative to independently designed projection heads.
neurips-2025-soft-task-aware-routing-of-.tldr: STAR routes invariant and equivariant learning through specialized experts to reduce redundant features and improve transfer performance.

paragraphs: People may want different levels of privacy when contributing data to an aggregate statistic. Personalized local differential privacy allows each participant to privatize their own data using a potentially different privacy parameter. This paper studies how to estimate a sum or mean accurately under that heterogeneous protection model.

The authors introduce two protocols with strong error guarantees. The first expresses its guarantee in terms of the data’s radius, making it suited to inputs centered around zero. The second uses the data’s diameter, extending the guarantee to collections located arbitrarily. This distinction matters because the location of a collection and the spread of its values are different properties.

The theoretical contribution supplies meaningful accuracy guarantees where prior work had fallen short for this personalized setting. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets report substantially better accuracy than existing methods while maintaining strong privacy. The two protocols offer complementary ways to connect estimation error to the geometry of the data, while allowing participants to retain different privacy requirements rather than adopting a single shared setting.
neurips-2025-sum-estimation-under-person.tldr: Two protocols provide strong sum and mean estimation guarantees while allowing each participant to choose a different local privacy level.

paragraphs: In-context learning lets a model infer a task from examples supplied in its input. Mamba has demonstrated this ability empirically, but its underlying learning mechanism is less theoretically understood than the corresponding Transformer setting. This paper studies a focused case: learning linear regression from context.

The authors analyze Mamba’s training dynamics using techniques designed for the nonconvex optimization problems created by its structure. They establish exponential convergence to an in-context learning solution and derive a loss bound comparable to a Transformer’s. These results concern the analyzed linear regression task, giving a concrete theoretical account of learning in that setting.

The mechanism revealed by the analysis is a variant of online gradient descent: Mamba can learn the latent function through successive updates as contextual examples arrive. The authors distinguish this from the gradient-descent emulation commonly used to interpret Transformer in-context learning. Simulations verify the theoretical findings. The contribution connects successful training, a quantitative loss guarantee, and an identifiable internal learning procedure within the same theoretical benchmark.
neurips-2025-trained-mamba-emulates-onli.tldr: For in-context linear regression, the paper proves convergence results and shows that trained Mamba can emulate a variant of online gradient descent.

paragraphs: Representation alignment can accelerate diffusion training by connecting a generator’s internal features to features from a vision transformer. Applying this idea to a U-Net requires architectural changes because its blocks have different roles, its spatial resolution changes, and its feature space differs from the encoder’s. U-REPA addresses those mismatches explicitly.

The authors identify the U-Net’s middle stage as the preferred alignment location based on observations involving skip connections. They pass U-Net features through multilayer perceptrons and then upsample them to address spatial differences. They also introduce a manifold loss that regularizes relative similarity between samples, responding to difficulties with direct token-by-token alignment.

Experiments report strong generation quality and substantially faster convergence. With a classifier-free guidance interval, U-REPA reaches FID below 1.5 on ImageNet at 256-by-256 resolution in 200 epochs or one million iterations. Under the stated sd-vae-ft-ema configuration, it outperforms REPA using half the total epochs. The results support adapting the alignment location, feature dimensions, and similarity objective to the U-Net architecture as a coordinated training strategy.
neurips-2025-u-repa-aligning-diffusion-u.tldr: U-REPA adapts representation alignment to diffusion U-Nets through middle-stage features, spatial resizing, and a sample-similarity loss.

paragraphs: Aligning a pretrained generative model with human preferences requires changing its outputs while retaining information from its original distribution. This paper focuses on flow matching models and the difficulty of combining efficient adaptation with probabilistically principled preservation of that prior. VGG-Flow approaches the problem through optimal control theory.

A flow model generates samples using a velocity field. The central idea is to match the difference between the adapted and pretrained velocity fields to the gradient of a value function. This turns the desired change in generative behavior into a gradient-matching objective. The method also uses first-order information from the reward model to inform adaptation.

A heuristic initialization of the value function helps the method adapt quickly. Experiments on Stable Diffusion 3 show effective, prior-preserving alignment under limited computational budgets. The empirical result supports the combined design: an optimal-control formulation supplies the relationship between velocity changes and value gradients, while reward information and initialization make adaptation practical. The demonstrated outcome concerns the tested text-to-image model and computational setting.
neurips-2025-value-gradient-guidance-for.tldr: VGG-Flow uses value-function gradients to efficiently align flow matching models while preserving information from their pretrained distribution.
